title: Rear Seat Backrest Cover - Coupe
introduction:
The coupe's rear backrest cover is held by a lower J-clip and hook-and-loop strips, with the latch strap passing through the cover. I think of it as a fitted jacket: undo the closures before trying to pull it off, or the foam underneath can become an unwilling passenger.

The job starts by removing the rear cushion and backrest. The instructions below explain that access through the linked procedures, then cover removal and refitting. The left-hand example also guides the similar right-hand seat.

requirements.category: Prepare the vehicle and protect yourself

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: Disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the vehicle. Otherwise, the vehicle can start remotely and cause personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Wear service protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts, including exposed seat hardware. Failing to use this protection can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Keep structural joints clear
items.detail: Follow every note and step in [Rear Seat Backrest - Coupe](#/document/G1692165). Do not place objects between the seat components and the vehicle body or within joints in the seat structure. Incorrect installation can cause improper seat operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury.

items.name: Preserve belt access
items.detail: During both backrest and cushion installation, keep safety-belt webbing untwisted and leave the belts and buckles accessible to the occupant. This requirement applies throughout reassembly, not just when the upholstery is finished.

edits.text: Remove the rear seat backrest before working on its cover. Refer to: [Rear Seat Backrest - Coupe](#/document/G1692165) (501-10B Rear Seats, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Start with [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168): move both front seats fully forward. At the front edge of the rear cushion, press in the locking tabs at both seating positions to release the cushion from the floor, then lift and remove it. Pulling the cushion up without pressing the tabs can damage them. With the cushion out, release the backrest's floor fastener at its outer lower mounting foot. The installation torque for that fastener is 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Disengage the backrest hinge eye from the end of the horizontal pivot pin, move the safety belt aside, and rotate the backrest toward the vehicle's outboard side. Lift its mounting foot off the floor stud and remove the backrest. These attachment locations and movements are shown in the linked backrest procedure.

edits.text: NOTE: The LH seat is shown; the RH seat uses a similar procedure.
edits.why: Use the illustrated attachment arrangement to orient yourself while allowing for the opposite side of the car.

edits.text: Open the backrest's lower J-clip by separating its interlocking lips along the lower edge.
edits.why: The first drawing highlights the opposing lower closure edges moving apart. This releases the bottom of the cover before the hook-and-loop attachments are separated.

edits.text: NOTICE: Separate the cover carefully from the hook-and-loop strips. Pulling carelessly can tear the strips away from the seat backrest foam pad.
edits.why: The intended separation is between the mating hook-and-loop surfaces. The foam's attached strips should remain with the foam rather than coming away with the cover.

edits.text: Carefully separate the backrest cover's hook-and-loop strips from the mating strips on the backrest foam. Feed the backrest latch strap through the opening in the cover so the cover is free of the strap, then remove the cover.
edits.why: I use the highlighted strip paths in the second drawing to track where the cover is still attached. The latch strap passes through a separate opening near the top; freeing it keeps the cover from hanging on the strap after the strips have separated.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: fit the cover over the backrest, route the latch strap out through its cover opening, join the matching hook-and-loop strips, and reconnect the lower J-clip. Reinstall the backrest, then the rear seat cushion, using their referenced procedures.
edits.why: For the backrest, reverse the access movements: lower the outer mounting foot over the floor stud, rotate the backrest inward with the safety belt held clear, engage the hinge on its pivot pin, then refit and tighten the floor fastener to its specified installation torque. Refit the cushion by reversing its removal and engaging its locking tabs with the floor. I finish by checking that the latch strap emerges through its opening, the cover closures are joined, belt webbing is untwisted, and belts and buckles remain accessible. Keep all seat-to-body and internal structural joints free of objects throughout reassembly.
